We need retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need propose steps: likely disconnection:

Target has sulfonamide linking a tolyl sulfonyl to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline.

We can think retrosynthetic steps:

1) Form sulfonamide: sulfonyl chloride + aniline. So disconnection: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the tolyl sulfonamide part). So precursor1: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CH3) and precursor2: aniline bearing the rest: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (i.e., a phenyl ring with side chain). Actually sulfonamide attaches to that phenyl ring at para position? The SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So tolyl ring (with methyl) attached to N of sulfonamide, which is attached to sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl ring (c2...). So sulfonamide formation between tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus step1: sulfonamide formation (forward: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide). Retrosynthesis: break S-N to give p-toluidine and aryl sulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl) where aryl is c2ccc(... )cc2.

2) The aryl sulfonyl chloride can be derived from the corresponding aryl sulfonic acid via chlorination (SO2Cl). But maybe we can consider that the aryl sulfonyl chloride is made from the aryl sulfonic acid which can be obtained from sulfonation of the aryl ring (electrophilic aromatic substitution). However we have limited steps (3 total). Another step: formation of amide from carboxylic acid and aniline (the side chain). The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl (aniline). So we can disconnect amide bond: break C-N to give carboxylic acid (trans-α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step2: amide coupling.

Thus precursor for amide: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid: C=CC(=O)O attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(/C=C/...)?? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring via the double bond: phenyl-CH=CH-COOH? Wait the SMILES: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N attached to phenyl ring at para position? The fragment: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So phenyl ring with side chain: CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually N attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N) is an aniline (para? not specified). So the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl via the double bond: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-... So the acid precursor would be phenyl-CH=CH-COOH (cinnamic acid) attached to phenyl ring? That's trans-cinnamic acid attached to phenyl? Actually the phenyl ring is the same as the one bearing the side chain; the side chain is attached to that phenyl at para position? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring (c2) has substituent /C=C/C(=O)N... So the unsaturated acid precursor would be c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2 (cinnamic acid attached to phenyl). So step2: amide formation between that acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we need aniline (aniline) as third precursor.

Thus we have three precursors: p-toluidine, aryl sulfonyl chloride (derived from phenyl with side chain), and aniline (c3ccccc3N). But we need three reactions total, so we need to generate aryl sulfonyl chloride from something via maybe sulfonation of phenyl ring (introduce SO2Cl). However we could consider that the aryl sulfonyl chloride is made from the same phenyl ring (c2) which also contains the side chain. So we need to form the sulfonyl chloride from that phenyl ring (maybe via chlorosulfonation of the phenyl). That's a reaction: aromatic sulfonyl chloride formation from benzene via chlorosulfonic acid (ClSO3H). So step3: chlorosulfonation of phenyl ring bearing side chain to give aryl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus overall three steps:

Step A (last forward): sulfonamide formation (p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride -> target).

Step B: amide coupling (cinnamic acid derivative + aniline -> aryl sulfonyl chloride precursor? Wait amide coupling yields the side chain attached to phenyl ring, which is part of the aryl sulfonyl chloride precursor. So the precursor after amide coupling is the phenyl ring with side chain (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2). This is the aryl sulfonyl chloride after step3.

Step C: chlorosulfonation of that phenyl ring (without sulfonyl) to introduce SO2Cl at para position relative to side chain? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to that phenyl ring at para to side chain? In SMILES, c2ccc(... )cc2, the sulfonyl group attaches to that phenyl via S(=O)(=O) attached to N of sulfonamide, not directly to ring. The sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl via S attached to N, not to ring. Wait the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring as part of the sulfonyl chloride: the aryl sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring (c2) via S(=O)(=O)Cl. So the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring at the position where the sulfonamide attaches (the same as the connection to p-toluidine). In SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring at the position where N attaches to S, not directly to ring. So the aryl sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring at that position (para to side chain? Not necessarily). So chlorosulfonation would install SO2Cl at that position.

Thus step3: chlorosulfonation of phenyl ring (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2) to give aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)/C=C/...?). Then step2 amide coupling to attach aniline to the side chain (cinnamic acid + aniline). Wait order: In retrosynthesis we go backwards: target -> break sulfonamide -> get p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (with side chain). Then break amide -> get cinnamic acid (aryl with side chain) + aniline. Then break sulfonyl chloride formation -> get phenyl ring with side chain (no sulfonyl) + chlorosulfonic acid? Actually we can consider that aryl sulfonyl chloride is derived from the phenyl ring via chlorosulfonation, which is a forward reaction: aromatic ring + ClSO3H -> aryl sulfonyl chloride. So retrosynthesis: aryl sulfonyl chloride -> aryl (same) + SO2Cl? But we need a precursor: the phenyl ring with side chain (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2). So step3: chlorosulfonation of that phenyl to give aryl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus we have three steps.

Now we need to find template IDs for each reaction type: sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide). amide coupling (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide). chlorosulfonation (aromatic ring + chlorosulfonic acid -> aryl sulfonyl chloride). We need to search template catalog for each.

Let's search for sulfonamide formation: functional_groups_broken maybe "sulfonamides"? Actually forward reaction forms sulfonamide, breaking sulfonyl chloride (S-Cl) and N-H. So broken functional groups: sulfonyl chloride? Not in list. But we can search by bonds broken/formed. Simpler: search for template with "sulfonamides" functional group formed. Use functional_groups_formed ["sulfonamides"].
